use: Review a .NET project for package versions, configuration, dependency injection, runtime settings and build safety. Use when asked to review or harden a .NET solution.

steps.note: Read the solution. Open the .sln, every .csproj, Directory.Packages.props if used, global.json, NuGet.config and any appsettings files.
Check packages. List each package and version.
Check configuration. Flag secrets in appsettings, connection strings with embedded passwords, and `Development` settings that would run in production.
Check dependency injection. Flag services registered with the wrong lifetime (a scoped service held by a singleton), and service locator calls inside business code.
Check runtime settings. Flag debug builds shipped, detailed errors enabled outside development, and `TreatWarningsAsErrors` turned off with many warnings ignored.
Check build and CI. Note the build commands, whether restore is locked, and whether tests run in the pipeline.

protocol.title: Read the solution
protocol.text: Open the .sln, every .csproj, Directory.Packages.props if used, global.json, NuGet.config and any appsettings files. Note the target frameworks and whether a framework is out of support.

protocol.title: Check packages
protocol.text: List each package and version. Flag versions with known advisories, packages pinned to floating versions (`*`), and duplicate packages with different versions.

protocol.title: Report
protocol.text: List each finding as `file`, with severity (high, medium or low), the problem and the fix. Mark what you did not run.
